I will keep my land in the usual Quzhou pattern: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same fields. I am 65, so I want a system I know well, can manage with machines, and can still count on for grain and cash. Here in Quzhou, this rotation fits the weather best: winter is dry and cold, summer is hot with most of the rain, so wheat uses the winter-spring irrigation and maize catches the summer rain. I will not spread myself across too many crops, because that raises labor, management trouble, and market risk. I will use an improved wheat seed and a hybrid maize seed, put most fertilizer on the wheat-maize rotation instead of chasing fancy crops, irrigate wheat more than maize, and keep pesticide use limited to what is needed for common field pests and diseases. I will use rotary tillage before wheat because it helps me prepare a clean seedbed after maize, and I will use no-tillage for maize into the wheat stubble to save time and moisture.
